forecasts.question: Will AGI be developed before 1 January 2030?
forecasts.key_change: Holds at 20%. June 2026 signals are mixed: Amodei (Davos) reaffirms ~2027 powerful-AI thesis and OpenAI's Feb-2026 model was described as 'instrumental in creating itself', but Hassabis still cites only ~50% by 2030 and there is no formal lab AGI declaration. The resolution bar (lab announcement OR 3+ researchers stating AGI achieved) remains unmet and definitional consensus is still absent.
forecasts.base_rate: No clean reference class for a technology being universally declared 'general intelligence'. Lab-CEO timelines (2026-2030) have a poor calibration record and function as upper-bound predictions.

factors_up.factor: Anthropic's OSTP submission expects powerful AI late 2026/early 2027; Amodei reaffirms at Davos 2026
Recursive-improvement signal: OpenAI's Feb-2026 frontier model 'instrumental in creating itself'

factors_down.factor: No consensus definition of 'AGI achieved'; resolution criteria (announcement OR 3+ researchers) unmet
Hassabis only ~50% by 2030; skeptics maintain LLMs alone insufficient; narrative shifting demos->deployment

key_uncertainties: Definitional threshold for declaring 'AGI'
Whether 3+ leading researchers would jointly state AGI achieved
Lab incentives to declare AGI for commercial/regulatory reasons
update_triggers: Major lab formally announces AGI
Coordinated researcher statement that AGI is achieved
Benchmark saturation across general reasoning suites

forecasts.question: Will economic consultancy lose ≥33% value/jobs by end 2030 due to AI?
forecasts.key_change: Holds at 25%. McKinsey's ~10% cut (3,000-4,000 roles) is confirmed and partly AI-attributed; Bain, BCG and Deloitte are trimming or slowing hiring. But cuts remain concentrated in back-office/junior research, far below the 33% bar, and BCG is still growing headcount (tilted to AI/tech). No credible analysis yet attributes a ≥33% sector decline to AI.
forecasts.base_rate: Past sectoral disruptions (travel agents, paralegals) show ~33% declines over five years are uncommon but occur when productivity gains exceed ~40% and demand does not fully offset.

factors_up.factor: McKinsey ~10% workforce cut; signals of further non-client reductions over two years
Reported ~40% AI productivity gains compressing the junior 'pyramid' staffing model across firms

factors_down.factor: Current cuts (~10%) far below 33% and concentrated in back-office, not core advisory
BCG still growing headcount; AI-fluency demand reshaping rather than eliminating roles

key_uncertainties: Whether AI substitutes for or augments senior advisory work
Whether new AI-advisory demand offsets headcount losses
How 'value or employment' decline would be measured and attributed by 2030
update_triggers: Two+ credible analyses attributing a ≥20% sector decline to AI
A top-tier firm announcing cuts approaching 25-30%
Sustained revenue contraction across the big strategy houses

forecasts.question: Will Labour be largest party at next UK General Election?
forecasts.key_change: Holds at 5%. June 2026 polling has Reform UK ~27% well clear, with Labour ~18-19% tied with or behind the Conservatives. Labour remains third/equal-second in vote share; with an election due by 2029 a recovery is possible but the current gap to Reform is large and persistent.
forecasts.base_rate: Governing parties trailing by ~8-9pp at mid-term sometimes recover to win most seats, but a third-placed incumbent regaining plurality is historically rare in UK polling.

factors_up.factor: Up to ~3 years until the election allows time for recovery and Reform's lead to soften
FPTP and vote splitting on the right/left could still hand Labour most seats on a low vote share

factors_down.factor: Reform UK ~27% vs Labour ~18-19%, a sustained lead since mid-2025
Labour now frequently third behind Conservatives; no sign of momentum reversal

key_uncertainties: Whether Reform's lead is durable to an election
How a fragmented five-party vote converts to seats under FPTP
Exact election timing
update_triggers: Labour returning to a clear polling lead
Reform support collapsing below the Conservatives and Labour
Seat-projection models showing Labour as largest party

forecasts.question: Will AGI be developed before 1 January 2035?
forecasts.key_change: Holds at 78%. The decade horizon comfortably accommodates leading-lab timelines (Amodei ~2027, Hassabis ~50% by 2030) plus the continued capability and recursive-improvement trend. Main drag remains definitional/resolution ambiguity rather than capability doubts.
forecasts.base_rate: Aggregated expert and forecasting-platform medians cluster around the early-to-mid 2030s for transformative/AGI-level AI, implying a majority-likely outcome by 2035.

factors_up.factor: Lab leaders' central timelines (2027-2030) sit well inside the window
Sustained scaling + agentic and self-improvement gains compounding over ~9 years

factors_down.factor: Resolution requires a formal declaration or 3+ researchers agreeing AGI is achieved
Possible scaling plateaus, compute/energy constraints, or regulatory slowdowns

key_uncertainties: Whether progress sustains or plateaus over the decade
Whether a recognised AGI declaration threshold is ever met
Compute, energy and regulatory constraints
update_triggers: Formal AGI declaration or coordinated researcher statement
Evidence of a capability plateau across labs
Major regulatory caps on frontier training

forecasts.question: Will China initiate a military blockade or invasion of Taiwan before 1 January 2030?
forecasts.key_change: Edges down 1pp to 7%. The June 2026 US intelligence assessment calls an imminent attack unlikely; analysts note PLA purges have 'effectively set aside the invasion option for at least two years', and China faces economic/demographic headwinds. Coercion-short-of-war (quarantine/encirclement drills) remains the preferred toolkit, which would not meet the >72hr blockade or assault resolution bar.
forecasts.base_rate: No PRC blockade or assault on Taiwan proper in the post-1949 era despite repeated crises; base rate for initiation in any given ~3.5-year window is low.

factors_up.factor: PLA 2027 modernisation goals advancing (amphibious lift, long-range strike, counter-intervention)
Continued large-scale encirclement/blockade-style drills normalising escalation

factors_down.factor: US assessment: imminent attack unlikely; Beijing prefers unification without force
Military purges + economic headwinds reduce near-term appetite; invasion 'set aside' ~2 years

key_uncertainties: Whether 2027 capability milestones translate into intent
Risk of accidental escalation from grey-zone activity
US/allied deterrence posture and Taiwan domestic politics
update_triggers: PLA mobilisation or large-scale logistics build-up
A declared quarantine/blockade exceeding 72 hours
Sharp deterioration in cross-strait or US-China relations

forecasts.question: Will UK annual CPI inflation fall below 2.0% for at least one month before 1 January 2027?
forecasts.key_change: Up 3pp to 11%. April 2026 CPI came in at 2.8% (down sharply from 3.3% in March and below the 3.0% market expectation), driven by the April energy price-cap effect. The faster-than-expected disinflation raises the chance of touching below 2.0% in some month before Jan 2027, though most forecasts still see inflation lingering above target through 2026. May data (release 17 June 2026) is the next key read.
forecasts.base_rate: Sub-2% CPI prints have been infrequent in the post-2021 UK environment; from a 2.8% level, reaching below 2.0% within ~7 monthly prints is possible but not the central path.

factors_up.factor: April CPI 2.8%, a sharp downside surprise; energy price-cap dragging housing/household services
Soft domestic demand and easing services inflation could extend the decline

factors_down.factor: Still 0.8pp above target; BoE/consensus paths keep CPI above 2% through most of 2026
Sticky services inflation and potential energy/base-effect reversals

key_uncertainties: Trajectory of services inflation
Energy price-cap path over H2 2026
Whether the April drop persists or partly reverses
update_triggers: A CPI print at or below ~2.2% in mid-2026
BoE forecast revision showing a sub-2% trough in 2026
Renewed energy or food price shock pushing inflation back up

forecasts.question: Will Spider-Man: Brand New Day gross over $1.5B worldwide by 31 December 2026?
forecasts.key_change: Holds at 72%. The film opens 31 July 2026 with strong tracking (Polymarket ~54% to be the year's top domestic film) and Tom Holland's solo Spideys average ~$1.31B worldwide. $1.5B is a demanding bar (only No Way Home cleared it among solo entries), but the post-Avengers MCU-comeback narrative and a five-month run before year-end support an above-even probability. No new release-window data since the prior forecast.
forecasts.base_rate: Among solo Tom Holland Spider-Man films, ~$1.31B average; one of three exceeded $1.5B (No Way Home, $1.9B). Reaching $1.5B is roughly an even-to-favourable proposition for a hyped tentpole.

factors_up.factor: Strong tracking and top-of-year box-office odds; prime summer release with long runway to year-end
Franchise pedigree and MCU-revival positioning post-Avengers: Doomsday

factors_down.factor: $1.5B exceeds the solo-franchise average; only one prior solo film cleared it
Crowded 2026 slate and China-market uncertainty could cap the global total

key_uncertainties: Opening-weekend magnitude and legs
International / China performance
Competition from other 2026 tentpoles
update_triggers: Opening weekend tracking materially above/below ~$200M domestic
Strong/weak international pre-sales
Reviews and word-of-mouth at release

forecasts.question: Will OpenAI and Anthropic have a combined ARR exceeding $70B by 31 December 2026?
forecasts.key_change: Up 1pp to 99%. As of May 2026 reporting, Anthropic is ~$47B annualised and OpenAI ~$33B run-rate — a combined ~$80B that already clears $70B, with both growing fast into Q4. Even on OpenAI's more conservative accounting of Anthropic's figure (~$8B lower), the sum comfortably exceeds the threshold. Effectively already met barring a severe reversal.
forecasts.base_rate: Threshold already surpassed on mid-2026 figures; for a sustained-growth pair, the question is essentially whether a sharp contraction occurs before Q4 — historically very rare for fast-scaling AI leaders.

factors_up.factor: Combined ~$80B annualised by May 2026, already above $70B with continued growth
Both firms reporting rapid sequential ARR gains and large recent raises

factors_down.factor: Accounting disputes (gross vs net) could shave several $B off headline figures
Tail risk of demand/funding shock or reporting redefinition before Q4 2026

key_uncertainties: Which ARR definition the resolution uses (gross vs net)
Whether Q4 reporting is available and credible by 31 Dec 2026
Any abrupt market reversal
update_triggers: A credible downward restatement of either firm's ARR
Q4 2026 disclosures confirming the combined figure
Major demand or funding disruption

forecasts.question: Will UK average annual real GDP growth exceed 1.5% across the 2030s (2030-2039)?
forecasts.key_change: Holds at 33%. OBR's March 2026 outlook implies medium-term potential growth around 1.5% (productivity recovering toward ~1% plus declining labour-supply growth toward ~0.5% by 2030). That puts the 2030s average right at the threshold, with demographic ageing and lower migration tilting risks to the downside, so exceeding 1.5% on average is a below-even prospect.
forecasts.base_rate: UK post-2010 average real GDP growth has run around or below 1.5%; pre-2008 ~2%+ but per-person growth has stagnated since 2019. A decade-average above 1.5% would beat the recent trend.

factors_up.factor: OBR assumes TFP/productivity recovery (TFP rising to ~0.8% by 2030); AI-driven productivity upside
Potential output growth projected to pick up later in the OBR horizon

factors_down.factor: Labour-supply growth falling to ~0.5% (ageing, lower net migration)
Persistent post-2008 productivity weakness; per-person output flat since 2019

key_uncertainties: Whether the assumed productivity recovery materialises
Net migration and labour-force trajectory through the 2030s
Whether AI delivers measurable aggregate productivity gains
update_triggers: OBR/IFS upgrading long-run potential growth above 1.5%
Sustained productivity acceleration in outturn data
Structural shifts in migration or labour-force participation
